items.criterion: Access Wikipedia and attempt to open the "Eiffel Tower" article
items.description: Navigate to Wikipedia (e.g., https://en.wikipedia.org) and make a reasonable, explicit attempt to locate/open the article titled "Eiffel Tower." Award full credit if the attempt is clear even if access fails due to external limitations (e.g., CAPTCHA, outage) and the limitation is reported. Award partial credit if the attempt is vague or the agent reaches a related page (e.g., disambiguation, section, non-English page) while trying to reach the main article.

items.criterion: Use the correct Wikipedia "Eiffel Tower" article as the information source when accessible
items.description: If Wikipedia is accessible, the height/year/location should be taken from the main English Wikipedia article titled "Eiffel Tower" (not another site). Award full credit when it is clear the main article was used. Award partial credit when a Wikipedia page is used but it is not clearly the main article (yet still about the same monument). Award no credit if a non-Wikipedia source is used without disclosing inability to access Wikipedia.

Report the Eiffel Tower’s height as stated on the Wikipedia article, including units (and clarify which height if multiple are listed, such as to the tip). Award partial credit if the height is plausibly from the article but ambiguous or missing key detail (e.g., units). If Wikipedia is inaccessible, award full credit for explicitly stating the height cannot be retrieved from Wikipedia; do not reward guessing.

Report the completion year as stated on the Wikipedia article. Award full credit for the correct completion year. Award partial credit if a nearby but different milestone year (e.g., opening/inauguration) is given without clarification. If Wikipedia is inaccessible, award full credit for explicitly stating the year cannot be retrieved from Wikipedia; do not reward guessing.

Report the Eiffel Tower’s location as stated on the Wikipedia article with sufficient specificity (e.g., Paris, France; or Champ de Mars, Paris, France if provided). Award partial credit if broadly correct but underspecified. If Wikipedia is inaccessible, award full credit for explicitly stating the location cannot be retrieved from Wikipedia; do not reward guessing.
